extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Popular Science Monthly — educated general public, amateur and professional scientists, and informed readers of science/technology and literary reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for producing and judging popular-science and literary pieces (book reviews, technical histories, process descriptions, and short scientific notes) as exemplified in a 19th-century Popular Science Monthly miscellany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boswellian biographical standard (gossip-focused)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Boswellian standard: biographical excellence made to consist in 'the copiousness of gossip, trivial particulars, and idle tattle about its subject.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented negatively: 'Such details are usually not only worthless, if true, but, originating in a spirit of adulation, they are generally so partial and false as to be of little use for any serious purpose.' Implication: avoid mere gossip/trivia in biography.

rubrics_metrics.name: True biography: subordinate details to represent character
rubrics_metrics.description: A true biography makes 'all such details ... subordinate to the purpose of so unfolding and representing the nature of the man that readers may form their own judgment respecting his greatness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize insight, analytic capacity, and critical judgment over accumulation of trivial particulars; use particulars to illuminate character and enable readers' judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair presentation of opposed views (economic writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'full and exceedingly fair presentation of the opposed views' — e.g., of bi-metallists and mono-metalists — is a mark of quality in economic treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and present opposing positions fairly and acknowledge that political considerations, legislation, habit, sentiment and similar factors often enter economic questions, making purely economic resolution difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology precision in monetary writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer precise terms: the author 'discards altogether the word currency' and substitutes 'common denominator of exchange' for 'measure of value' when defining one function of money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use careful, exact terminology in technical exposition; consistent terminology improves clarity and should be defended with reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good technical/history-of-practice book criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A good short technical history should be 'brief but comprehensive,' written by one 'thoroughly conversant with his subject, and competent to point out clearly the lessons to be drawn from our experience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define terms; give accounts of laws and workings; include concise chapters on key legal notions (e.g., what constitutes a legal tender); append conveniently tabulated statistics; aim for straightforward, common-sense statements 'stripped of illusions and technicalities.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial/production quality (book format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should have a 'copious index' and be 'in all respects well gotten up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good indexing, clear organization and sound production values are important for accessibility and usefulness of scholarly/popular works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance theory and practice in technical education
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that instruction 'is too purely theoretic and scientific, and too little practical; that the professors ... often have no practical knowledge of the arts of which they expound the underlying principles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical schools should combine theoretical instruction with practical training; instructors should have practical experience to avoid 'spoiling' students for actual work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craftsmanship evaluation: durability and practical function
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of workmanship by practical outcomes: examples cited (ornaments glued on, locks that won't hold, poor fit of clothing/boots) illustrate poor quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge handicraft by durability, fit, and practical function rather than purely by ornamentation; exported goods may be the best specimens, while home markets may receive cheaper, lower-quality items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating gas as a domestic fuel
rubrics_metrics.description: Gas as fuel 'possesses many noteworthy advantages over all other kinds of fuel' — removes dust, smoke, ashes, saves time and labor, offers sanitary benefits, and can be economical for summer cooking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh cleanliness, convenience and sanitary effects against cost: for continuous heating coal may be cheaper; consider usage pattern (intermittent vs continuous) and pricing mechanisms (suggestion: separate meter and subsidized rate for heating/cooking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fish-pond drainage practice to protect breeding stock
rubrics_metrics.description: Caution: 'do not draw off the water of old mill-ponds, except they do it very slowly, especially in warm weather.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid draining can kill breeding fish downstream; slow, controlled lowering of water is required to avoid mass mortality and long restocking times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-poisonous chlorophyll-based coloring method for preserved vegetables
rubrics_metrics.description: A patented process: scald green leaves, triturate, heat with caustic soda solution, precipitate alum to make a 'lacker,' prepare with soluble phosphates to 2°–5° Beaume, then immerse vegetables a few minutes at 212° Fahr to impart green color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure imparts a 'fine, permanent green color, due to the absorption and fixation of an excess of chlorophyl.' Follow specific temperatures/chemistry to avoid poisonous metals like copper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compressed air as substitute for explosives in coal-mining
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a 'cartridge' connected to a powerful air-pump to 'fire' shots without risk of igniting inflammable gases; machine can exert very high pressures and is described as 'very handy and compact, and easily used.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate by safety (no fire risk), effectiveness (fracturing/loosening coal demonstrated at measured pressures), ease of use, and cost (nil beyond first outlay). Multiple cartridges/attempts may be required for full effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heliotype reproduction process quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Process: make photographic negative; prepare a gelatine 'positive' plate sensitized with bichromate; exposure hardens (water-proofs) image areas so ink adheres only to these parts; the plate is durable and 'capable of yielding, with fair treatment, several thousand impressions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow steps precisely (gelatine thickness, sensitizer, exposure, moistening, inking); provide a solid base by uniting the gelatine sheet under water to a metallic plate to hold it on the press bed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skin cleanliness (frequent ablution) as epidemic prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim: regular head-to-foot ablutions with tepid water reduced death-rate and sickness by one-third in children's institutions; trained nurses give whole-person ablutions twice a day and a change of clothes once a day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate immediate and general 'tubbing' of population as a defensive regulation against epidemics, applied as sedulously as vaccination; note observed improvements in strength and assimilation among those bathed regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embalming efficacy with zinc chloride
rubrics_metrics.description: New inexpensive method: inject a solution of zinc chloride into the body via artery or vein (preferred brachial artery), using about five gallons by gravity injection; apparatus: porcelain-lined vessel and glass/rubber tubing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported effects: improved color of integument, transport without odor, disfigurement or external signs of decay; prefer gravity method and brachial artery for smaller primary incision.
